thesis: AeroVironment, Inc. (NASDAQ: AVAV) designs and produces unmanned aircraft systems, loitering munitions, and related defense technologies for the U.S. Department of Defense and allied governments. **[Fact]** FY2026 revenue was **$1,976.8 million**, more than double FY2025's **$820.6 million**, primarily because the company closed the **BlueHalo** acquisition on May 1, 2025 and now reports two operating segments: **Autonomous Systems (AxS)** and **Space, Cyber and Directed Energy (SCDE)**. **[Fact]** Flagship products include the Switchblade family of loitering munitions, small UAS, and BlueHalo-derived space, cyber, and missile-defense offerings. **[Fact]** Funded backlog was approximately **$1,183 million** at April 30, 2026, up from **$726.6 million** a year earlier, with management expecting about **85%** of that backlog to convert to revenue in fiscal 2027. **[Inference]** The equity today is a leveraged defense-growth platform whose near-term GAAP earnings are dominated by acquisition accounting, not underlying demand.
why_market_wrong: The market may be capitalizing a **post-BlueHalo growth narrative** (loitering munitions demand, broader defense-tech portfolio, $1.2B funded backlog) while underweighting **integration-year cash economics**: FY2026 GAAP operating loss of **$311 million**, **negative** operating cash flow of **$78.4 million**, **$204 million** of intangible amortization, a **$241 million** goodwill impairment tied to the terminated SCAR space program, and **$729 million** of long-term debt. **[Inference]** Segment adjusted EBITDA of roughly **$286 million** (AxS **$288.7 million** plus SCDE **-$2.6 million**) shows operating demand, but reported owner cash is still negative and normalized free cash per share is far below the current share price. **[Inference]** Lock-up releases on **~17.4 million** BlueHalo seller shares (40% May 2026, 30% November 2026, remainder May 2027) may also create a supply overhang not visible in backlog headlines.
